scope: Theorem 6.6 (Address lemma) of the manuscript “Goldfeld's analytic density conjecture and the 2-converse for elliptic curves” (preprints/Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 006 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c417858c9fe566da), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 44. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume the contraction, isolation, and whole-prime omission rules of Proposition 5.5, or the same rules for another symbol, together with the realization freedoms of Lemma 6.1. Let b ≥ 1 and consider either of the following terminal arrangements: 1. One symbol on a nonempty set of always active terminals, whose polynomial in the independent pair bits is nonzero. 2. One or two symbols on terminals with nonzero linear activations, including a terminal for every nonzero linear form. At each x ̸= 0, each symbol separately is a nonzero polynomial in the active bits. The symbols may have stationary external data and may read compatible projections of a common graph. At every x ̸= 0, assume that the active terminal data and the stationary external data obey each required filter. Then finitely many primary auxiliaries with nonzero linear activations, and one realizable assignment of graph bits, make all the symbols 1 at every x ̸= 0. No auxiliary is present at 0. All may satisfy fixed splitting and neutral-incidence conditions included in their primary type. A nonzero evaluation or a nonzero iterated edge difference suffices for the polynomial hypothesis. In particular, a partition as in Definition 6.2 suffices in the stationary case.
